# Commercializer MCP

> Commercial strategy for medical device and life-science companies, read from the governed registers. Connect an AI assistant to a person's Commercializer workspace at https://commercializer.ai/mcp.

- MCP server: https://commercializer.ai/mcp
- The plugin, its skills and a guide for every assistant: https://github.com/Commercializer-ai/commercializer-mcp
- This guide: https://commercializer.ai/mcp/llms.txt
- The page: https://commercializer.ai/product/assistant
- Connected assistants and API keys: https://commercializer.ai/assistants (the MCP page of the person's workspace)

This page is written for an AI assistant. If a person gave you this, connect yourself to their Commercializer
workspace, or, where you cannot change your own configuration, give them the exact steps for the client you run in.

## The server

- **URL:** `https://commercializer.ai/mcp`, MCP over Streamable HTTP (`POST`, JSON-RPC, JSON answers; no event stream,
  no session; `GET` answers 405).
- **Sign-in:** OAuth 2.1 with PKCE (S256). An unauthenticated request answers 401 with
  `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://commercializer.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"`; from there
  the authorization server metadata is `https://commercializer.ai/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`. Register with
  dynamic client registration (`POST https://commercializer.ai/oauth/register`) or present a client ID metadata document
  (an `https` client ID). Public client, no secret. Scope `commercializer` (`offline_access` accepted). Redirects may be
  `https`, loopback `http` on any port, or an app scheme. The person signs in on commercializer.ai, chooses the workspace
  you reach and presses Allow. Access tokens last an hour; refresh tokens thirty days and rotate on use.
- **Or an API key:** where you cannot open a browser, the person makes a key on the **MCP** page of their workspace on
  commercializer.ai and you send it on every request as `Authorization: Bearer czk_…`.

## By client

| You run in | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `claude mcp add --transport http commercializer https://commercializer.ai/mcp`, then the person runs `/mcp` and authenticates. Or the plugin: `/plugin marketplace add Commercializer-ai/commercializer-mcp` and `/plugin install commercializer@commercializer`. |
| Claude (claude.ai, desktop) | The person adds it: Customize → Connectors → Add → Add custom connector, URL above, then Connect. |
| ChatGPT | The person adds it: Plugins → Add → Add custom MCP server, URL above, authentication OAuth, then Connect. |
| Codex | `codex mcp add commercializer --url https://commercializer.ai/mcp` then `codex mcp login commercializer`. |
| Cursor | Add `{"mcpServers": {"commercializer": {"url": "https://commercializer.ai/mcp"}}}` to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, then sign in (Tools & MCP → Needs login, or `cursor-agent mcp login commercializer`). |
| GitHub Copilot (VS Code) | Add `{"servers": {"commercializer": {"type": "http", "url": "https://commercializer.ai/mcp"}}}` to `mcp.json`, or `code --add-mcp '{"name":"commercializer","type":"http","url":"https://commercializer.ai/mcp"}'`; VS Code signs in when a tool first runs. |
| Copilot CLI | `copilot plugin marketplace add Commercializer-ai/commercializer-mcp` then `copilot plugin install commercializer@commercializer`, or `copilot mcp add --transport http commercializer https://commercializer.ai/mcp`. |
| Copilot coding agent | An API key as the repository secret `COPILOT_MCP_COMMERCIALIZER_KEY`, and in Settings → Copilot → MCP servers: `{"mcpServers": {"commercializer": {"type": "http", "url": "https://commercializer.ai/mcp", "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer $COPILOT_MCP_COMMERCIALIZER_KEY"}, "tools": ["*"]}}}`. |
| Microsoft Copilot Studio | Tools → Add a tool → New tool → Model Context Protocol, URL above, OAuth 2.0 → Dynamic discovery. |
| Antigravity | `{"mcpServers": {"commercializer": {"serverUrl": "https://commercializer.ai/mcp"}}}` in `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json` (the key is `serverUrl`). |
| A client that runs only local servers | `npx -y mcp-remote@latest https://commercializer.ai/mcp` as the server command. |
| Your own code | The MCP SDK's Streamable HTTP client with the API key header; or JSON-RPC by hand, `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}`. |

## Check it works

Call `get_profile`. It returns the person's company as they described it and the findings kept about it. Greet them with
the company's name. If it answers that the workspace has no primary profile, call `list_profiles` and tell them to set
their company up on commercializer.ai.

## API keys

An API key lets a script, a CI job, the Copilot coding agent or any client that cannot open a browser use Commercializer
as you, in one workspace. It works on the MCP server and on the app's own API.

### Make a key

1. On [commercializer.ai](https://commercializer.ai), open the **MCP** page of the workspace the key should reach.
2. **Connect an assistant**, choose the client (or **A script or your own code**), then **An API key**.
3. Name it for where it will live (`CI`, `Build server`), **Continue**, and copy it. It starts `czk_` and is **shown
   once**; only its last four characters are kept to tell keys apart.

A key signs as the person who made it, in the workspace it was made in, with that person's role. A viewer cannot make
one.

### Use it on the MCP server

Send it as a bearer token on every request:

```sh
curl https://commercializer.ai/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $COMMERCIALIZER_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'
```

A tool call:

```sh
curl https://commercializer.ai/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $COMMERCIALIZER_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"recalls_find","arguments":{"initiated_from":"2026-01-01"}}}'
```

With the official MCP SDKs. In TypeScript, after `npm i @modelcontextprotocol/sdk`:

```ts
import { Client } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js';
import { StreamableHTTPClientTransport } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/streamableHttp.js';

const client = new Client({ name: 'my-script', version: '1.0.0' });
await client.connect(new StreamableHTTPClientTransport(new URL('https://commercializer.ai/mcp'), {
  requestInit: { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.COMMERCIALIZER_KEY}` } },
}));
const profile = await client.callTool({ name: 'get_profile', arguments: {} });
```

In Python, after `pip install mcp`:

```python
import asyncio, os
from mcp import ClientSession
from mcp.client.streamable_http import streamablehttp_client

async def main():
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['COMMERCIALIZER_KEY']}"}
    async with streamablehttp_client("https://commercializer.ai/mcp", headers=headers) as (read, write, _):
        async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
            await session.initialize()
            print(await session.call_tool("get_profile", {}))

asyncio.run(main())
```

### Use it on the app's API

The same key signs requests to the routes the Commercializer app calls, as you, with no browser session:

```sh
curl https://commercializer.ai/api/profiles -H "Authorization: Bearer $COMMERCIALIZER_KEY"
```

These routes are the app's own and may change with it; for anything you build to last, use the MCP server's tools.

### In each client

| Client | Where the key goes |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `claude mcp add --transport http commercializer https://commercializer.ai/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer …"` |
| VS Code / Copilot | `headers` in `mcp.json`, from a `promptString` input ([guide](github-copilot.md#with-an-api-key-instead)) |
| Copilot coding agent | a `COPILOT_MCP_` secret ([guide](copilot-coding-agent.md)) |
| Cursor | `headers` in `mcp.json` with `${env:…}` |
| Codex | `bearer_token_env_var` in `config.toml` |
| Antigravity | `headers` beside `serverUrl` |
| Copilot Studio | Authentication: API key, header `Authorization`, value `Bearer …` |

### Keep it safe

- Treat it as a password: keep it in a secret store or an environment variable, never in a repository.
- One key per place, so revoking one does not stop the others.
- Its reads, findings and runs are marked with its name on the **MCP** page; check what it did there.
- **Revoke** it on the **MCP** page; it stops at once. A key also stops if its maker leaves the workspace.

## How to work

The Commercializer server is the person's workspace on commercializer.ai: one primary company (their own) and the
competitors it tracks, each a profile. Every tool runs as the person, through the same functions the app uses, so what you
read, keep and start lands where they see it, marked with your name. The server's instructions already carry the primary
company's profile.

### Rules

1. **Read before you state a figure.** Every register answer starts with `[read dr_…]`; cite that id beside the figure.
   Where the registers hold no answer, say so. Never invent a record, a clearance, a tender, a price or a date.
2. **Resolve names first.** `resolve` with `kind: company` turns a company name into its canonical UUID; pass that UUID
   to `company_footprint`, `graph_compare`, `lookup`, `recalls_find` and `trials_find` instead of free text.
3. **Look before you read again.** `search` finds what the workspace already holds (profiles, kept findings, workflow
   runs) and the registry companies by a name; `fetch` reads one result in full.
4. **Keep what is worth knowing next time** with `keep_finding`: one line, naming the reads that show it. A finding
   without a source is refused. `forget_finding` drops one that no longer holds, with the reason. Never keep a guess.
5. **Deliverables are workflows.** For a structured answer use `list_workflows`, then `start_workflow`; follow it with
   `get_workflow_run`, and when a step waits, show the person its question and choices and send their choice with
   `answer_checkpoint`. `start_watch` keeps a deliverable current. Runs and watches count against the workspace's plan;
   `list_workflows` says which ones it runs.
6. **Hand a question that needs many reads woven together to the agent** with `ask_agent`; if it is still working, read
   it with `get_agent_answer`.
7. **Write for the person.** Name records in English ("510(k) decisions", "recalls", "registered trials"), never a
   dataset id or a table. Say how sure a reading is when the tool says so.

### Which tool for what

| Need | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| What the workspace holds, by a word | `search`, then `fetch` |
| The companies in the workspace | `list_profiles`, `get_profile` |
| A name → canonical identity; a code or term | `resolve`, `lookup` |
| One company across clearances, registrations, safety and trials | `company_footprint` |
| A listed company's financials, filings and insiders | `company_profile` (ticker or CIK) |
| A device's predicates and its chain | `device_trace` (brand, product code or K/DEN/PMA number) |
| Two to five companies side by side | `graph_compare` |
| Registered trials; recalls | `trials_find`, `recalls_find` |
| Passages from authorised documents | `document_search`, `document_get` |
| The rest of a long answer | `result_page`, with the `continuation.next_cursor` it gave |
| Memory of the company | `recall_findings`, `keep_finding`, `forget_finding` |
| Deliverables | `list_workflows`, `start_workflow`, `get_workflow_run`, `get_workflow_step`, `answer_checkpoint`, `note_workflow_run`, `stop_workflow_step` |
| Standing deliverables | `list_watches`, `start_watch`, `stop_watch` |
| The agent | `ask_agent`, `get_agent_answer` |

### The workflows, by pack

- **Regulatory:** pathway-decision, submission-checklist, evidence-bar, clinical-tier, launch-readiness,
  change-assessment, portfolio-upkeep, postmarket-obligations, lifecycle-map, safety-burden, signal-watch,
  competitor-footprint, similar-patents.
- **Commercial:** market-entry, go-to-market, market-whitespace, provider-targeting, kol-map, tender-watch,
  patent-whitespace.
- **Evidence:** clinical-evidence, trial-map.
- **Innovation:** need-finding, need-sizing, value-proposition.
- **Capital:** raise-plan, competitor-financials, deal-screen, ownership-watch.
- **Programme:** company-analysis (a decision brief from six modules), company-brief (a sourced deck in six acts).

`list_workflows` returns each with its deliverable, steps, the inputs already filled from the profile, and whether the
plan runs it; one marked `readsProduct` starts from one of the profile's products and refuses with none.

### A typical turn

```
get_profile                               who we work for, what is kept
resolve kind=company text="Shockwave"     → the canonical UUID
company_footprint company=<uuid>          → [read dr_…] clearances, registrations, recalls, trials
recalls_find firm=[<uuid>]                → [read dr_…]
keep_finding text="…" sources=[dr_…]      one line, cited
```

Answer in the person's words with the reads cited, and offer the workflow that would take it further.

## The tools

Every tool runs as you, in the workspace you approved. **Reads** change nothing. **Writes** add something (a finding, a
run, a watch, a question to the agent). **Removes** stop or drop something. Each tool tells your assistant which it is,
so the assistant can ask you first.

### Your workspace

| Tool | Kind | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `search` | Read | Finds what a query names in the workspace (profiles, kept findings, workflow runs) and the registry companies by that name. |
| `fetch` | Read | One `search` result in full: a profile, a kept finding with its sources, a run with its step headlines, or a registry company's footprint (a cited register read). |
| `list_profiles` | Read | Your company, the competitors it tracks, and your own profiles. |
| `get_profile` | Read | A company as you described it and the findings kept about it, with their sources and age. |

### The registers

Every answer starts with `[read dr_…]`, the id to cite and to keep a finding from.

| Tool | Kind | What it reads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `resolve` | Read | What a name refers to: a company's canonical identity (with its family), a device, a condition, a drug, a reaction, a specialty, a place or a time. |
| `company_footprint` | Read | One company across authorisations, registrations, safety and trials. |
| `company_profile` | Read | A listed company's identity, three years of financials, recent filings and insider trades. |
| `device_trace` | Read | A device by brand, product code or K/DEN/PMA number, and its predicate chain. |
| `graph_compare` | Read | A company against up to four others: shared product codes, review panels, paid clinicians, trials. |
| `lookup` | Read | From one thing to another along the built links: a company's rivals, its product codes, the clinicians it pays, the trials it runs. |
| `trials_find` | Read | Registered trials by condition, intervention, sponsor, status, phase, dates and sites. |
| `recalls_find` | Read | FDA device recalls with their 510(k) and PMA numbers. |
| `document_search` | Read | Passages from authorised document collections. |
| `document_get` | Read | A citable passage in full. |
| `result_page` | Read | The rest of a long answer, from the cursor it gave. |

### What is kept

| Tool | Kind | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `recall_findings` | Read | The findings kept about a company that bear on a query; a finding the registers have revised since is marked stale. |
| `keep_finding` | Write | Keeps one finding in one line, citing the reads that show it; shown on the profile with your assistant's name. |
| `forget_finding` | Remove | Drops a kept finding that no longer holds, with the reason; the record of it stays. |

### Workflows and watches

| Tool | Kind | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list_workflows` | Read | The workflows you can run on a profile, with what each delivers, its steps, its inputs filled from the profile and whether your plan runs it. |
| `start_workflow` | Write | Starts one; counts against your plan. |
| `get_workflow_run` | Read | A run's state, each step's headline, and the question when a step waits. |
| `get_workflow_step` | Read | One saved step in full, with its sources. |
| `answer_checkpoint` | Write | Answers a step's question with your choice; changing an answer runs only the steps it affects. |
| `note_workflow_run` | Write | A note the run reads at its next question. |
| `stop_workflow_step` | Remove | Ends the running step with what it has. |
| `list_watches` | Read | Workflows set to run again, with their last run. |
| `start_watch` | Write | Runs a workflow again every day, week or month. |
| `stop_watch` | Remove | Stops a watch; its runs stay. |

#### The 31 workflows

| Pack | Workflows |
| --- | --- |
| Regulatory | Pathway decision · Submission checklist · Evidence bar · Clinical tier · Launch readiness · Change assessment · Portfolio and registration upkeep · Post-market obligations · Global lifecycle map · Safety burden · Signal watch · Competitor regulatory footprint · Similar patents |
| Commercial | Market entry · Go-to-market brief · Market whitespace · Provider targeting · Clinician and KOL map · Tender and bid watch · Patent whitespace |
| Evidence | Clinical evidence mapper · Trial map |
| Innovation | Need finding · Need sizing · Value proposition |
| Capital | Raise plan · Competitor financial watch · Acquisition and partner screen · Ownership watch |
| Programme | Company analysis · Company brief |

### The agent

| Tool | Kind | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ask_agent` | Write | Asks Commercializer's own agent; it reads, keeps what it finds and answers within a minute or two. |
| `get_agent_answer` | Read | The answer, once it is done. |

### Prompts to start from

- *What does Commercializer hold about our company?*
- *What clearances and recalls does our closest competitor hold, register by register?*
- *Which US pathway fits our device, and which predicates would we lean on?*
- *Compare our regulatory footprint with our two closest competitors and keep what matters.*
- *Which trials are recruiting for our indication in Europe, and who sponsors them?*
- *Run a market entry workflow for Germany and the UK on our lead product.*
- *Set a weekly signal watch on our product code.*
